q: Which equipment is used to level and compact freshly poured concrete, creating a smooth and even surface?
n: A screeding machine (vibratory or laser screed) strikes off fresh concrete to grade and consolidates the surface. That gives a level, even slab ready for finishing. Source: ACI 302.1R (Concrete Floor and Slab Construction – Strikeoff and Screeding).

q: What is the solid or semisolid residue obtained from the partial evaporation or fractional distillation of tar?
n: Pitch is the dark solid or semisolid residue left after distilling coal tar or wood tar. Bitumen and asphalt come from petroleum. Source: ASTM D8 (Standard Terminology – Pitch); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: Which of the following is a thermoset material commonly used in construction?
n: Epoxy is a thermoset: it cures by irreversible cross-linking and cannot be remelted. Polyethylene, PVC and polystyrene are thermoplastics. Source: Callister, Materials Science and Engineering (Polymers); Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction.

q: Which of the following is a thermoplastic material commonly used in construction applications?
n: Polyethylene is a thermoplastic that softens when heated and can be reshaped. It is used for vapor barriers, pipes and membranes. Bakelite, epoxy and melamine are thermosets. Source: Callister, Materials Science and Engineering (Polymers).

q: In construction, what is the term for the layer of soil or rock that provides adequate bearing capacity for the load transferred by piles?
n: The bearing stratum is the soil or rock layer with enough capacity to support the loads transferred by piles. End-bearing piles are driven to it. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Pile Foundations); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 3.

q: Mortar grade with the least strength.
n: Masonry mortar types in descending strength are M, S, N, O and K. Type K is the weakest and is used only for non-load-bearing work. Source: ASTM C270 (Mortar for Unit Masonry).

q: What safety procedure is used to ensure that machinery is properly shut off and not started up again before the completion of maintenance or servicing work?
n: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) isolates energy sources and locks and tags them. Machinery then cannot be restarted until maintenance or servicing is finished. Source: DOLE OSHS Rule 1210 and DO 198-18 (Construction Safety); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147.

q: What is the primary purpose of a deadman switch in construction equipment?
o: provide a backup power source in case of failure
automatically stop the machine when the operator releases control
enhance the speed of machine operation
maintain constant power output during operation
n: A deadman switch must be held by the operator. If the operator releases it, through incapacity or leaving the controls, the machine stops automatically. Source: DOLE OSHS (Construction Safety – Equipment Controls); ISO 12100 (Safety of Machinery).

q: Which government department is primarily responsible for implementing Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) regulations in the construction industry?
o: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)
n: The Department of Labor and Employment implements and enforces Occupational Safety and Health standards, including construction safety. Source: RA 11058 (OSH Law) and DOLE DO 198-18; DOLE Occupational Safety and Health Standards.

q: How many hours is the Construction Occupational Safety and Health (COSH) training required in the Philippines for site safety officers?
n: Construction safety officers must complete the 40-hour Construction Occupational Safety and Health (COSH) training accredited by DOLE. Source: DOLE DO 13 s.1998 and DO 198-18 (IRR of RA 11058).

q: What term is used to describe construction activities that involve open flames, sparks, or the generation of heat, requiring special safety precautions to prevent fires?
n: Hot work is any work producing flames, sparks or heat, such as welding, cutting, brazing and grinding. It needs a hot-work permit and fire precautions. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Hot Work); NFPA 51B.

q: Why is quarter sawing considered better than plain sawing when cutting hardwood logs?
o: It produces more wood from each log
It is faster and requires less effort
It makes boards more stable and less likely to warp
n: Quarter-sawn boards have growth rings at a steep angle to the face. They shrink less across the width, resist cupping and warping, and are more stable. Plain sawing gives more yield, faster. Source: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook, Ch. 5; Hoadley, Understanding Wood.

q: In construction, what is the primary purpose of the tool commonly known as "pitik”?
o: To mark straight reference lines on surfaces
To drill precise holes in concrete
n: "Pitik" is the local name for the chalk line. Stretched and snapped, it marks a straight reference line on floors, walls and boards. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Layout tools); construction trade terminology.

q: A concrete-filled, thin-walled tubular steel column used for vertical support in buildings.
n: A lally column is a thin-walled steel pipe filled with concrete, used as a vertical support such as under basement beams. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Lally Column); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which of the following is a horizontal element?
n: A batter board is the horizontal board nailed to stakes outside the building corners. It holds the strings that mark the building lines. Stakes and piles are vertical. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 1 (Layout); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: Which of the following is the ideal foundation in loose sand?
n: Loose sand has low bearing capacity and settles. Loads are spread over a mat or carried down by piles to firmer strata. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Mat and Pile Foundations).

q: What type of Fire Detection and Alarm System (FDAS) provides the exact location of a fire within a building?
n: In an addressable FDAS, each device has a unique address. The panel identifies the exact device and location in alarm. Conventional systems only identify a zone. Source: NFPA 72 (Fire Alarm and Signaling Code); RA 9514 RIRR.

q: What is the standard color of a manual call point (MCP)?
n: Manual call points (MCPs) are red, so they are instantly recognizable as fire alarm devices. Source: BS EN 54-11 (Manual Call Points); NFPA 72.

q: Which type of HVAC system is most commonly used in residential and small commercial applications due to its cost-effectiveness and modular design?
n: Direct-expansion (DX) systems, the split and window units, cool the air directly with refrigerant. They are modular and economical, so they dominate homes and small commercial spaces. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – HVAC Systems and Equipment (Unitary/DX Systems).

q: What is the purpose of night setback in HVAC systems?
o: to maximize the solar energy collected
n: Night setback raises the cooling setpoint (or lowers the heating setpoint) when a building is unoccupied, to save energy. Source: ASHRAE Standard 90.1 (Setback Controls); ASHRAE Handbook – HVAC Applications.

q: A supply vent with adjustable louvers to regulate airflow.
n: A register is a supply outlet with a grille and adjustable louvers or a damper, so airflow can be directed and regulated. A grille has no damper. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals (Air Diffusion); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: What term describes the gradual downward movement of a structure due to the compression of soil beneath its foundation?
n: Settlement is the downward movement of a structure as the soil beneath its foundation compresses or consolidates. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Settlement); NSCP 2015, Ch. 3.

q: What type of bolt is most suitable for connecting a steel beam to a reinforced concrete (RC) beam?
n: Anchor bolts, cast-in or post-installed, fix steel members to concrete. They are the connector for joining a steel beam to an RC beam or wall. Machine and carriage bolts join steel or wood to steel or wood. Source: ACI 318 / NSCP 2015, Ch. 4 (Anchoring to Concrete); AISC Design Guide 1.

q: What is the purpose of temperature bars?
n: Temperature (shrinkage) bars are distribution steel placed perpendicular to the main bars. They control and minimize cracks from shrinkage and temperature change. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 424.4; ACI 318.

q: In a continuous concrete slab, where is the greatest negative moment typically located?
n: In a continuous slab, the largest negative moments occur over the interior supports. The top bars are concentrated there. Positive moment peaks near midspan. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 406.5 (Approximate Moment Coefficients); MacGregor & Wight, Reinforced Concrete.

q: In a one-way slab, what is the orientation of the main reinforcement bars?
n: A one-way slab bends mainly across its short span. The main bars run parallel to the short span, which is perpendicular to the long side. Temperature bars run the other way. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 407 (One-way Slabs); MacGregor & Wight, Reinforced Concrete.

q: What can be used in wood surface to prevent discoloration from the inside of the wood?
n: Tannin-blocking (stain-resistant) primers or paints stop water-soluble tannins in woods like narra and cedar from bleeding through and discoloring the finish. Source: PDCA Painting Standards (Tannin Bleed); MPI Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: What is the term for the angular cut made at the end of beams or joists to prevent structural damage during a fire?
n: A fire cut is an angled cut at the end of a joist or beam bearing in masonry. If the member burns through and falls, it rotates out without levering the wall over. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Fire Cut); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Mosaic work using small pieces of wood.
n: Parquetry is mosaic work of small pieces of wood laid in geometric patterns, mainly for floors. Marquetry and intarsia are pictorial veneer and inlay work. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Parquetry); NWFA.

q: What is the ideal woodworking joint for connecting two profiled moldings, ensuring a tight and seamless fit?
n: A coped joint cuts one molding to the reverse profile of the other, so it fits tightly over its face. It stays closed at inside corners even if the wood moves. Source: Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Finish Carpentry); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10.

q: In a mortise and tenon joint, what is the name of the projecting part that fits into the cavity?
n: In a mortise-and-tenon joint, the tenon is the projecting tongue that fits into the mortise, the cavity. Source: Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Joinery); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which type of joinery involves cutting two pieces of material at an angle, usually 45 degrees, to form a corner joint?
n: A miter joint cuts both pieces at an angle, usually 45°, so they form a corner. Source: Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Joinery); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What is the term for the upper surface of a sill block that is inclined to shed rainwater away from a building?
n: The wash is the sloped top surface of a sill, coping or cornice. It sheds rainwater away from the wall. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Wash); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which of the following is an engineered wood product commonly used in construction and furniture making?
n: Plywood is an engineered wood panel made of cross-laminated veneers. Teak and mahogany are solid timbers, and bamboo is a natural grass. Source: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook, Ch. 11 (Wood-Based Composites).

q: ASHRAE Minimum ACH for residential spaces.
n: ASHRAE Standard 62 (62-1989 and early 62.2) set a minimum of 0.35 air changes per hour for residential living areas. Source: ASHRAE Standard 62-1989 / 62.2 (Ventilation for Acceptable Indoor Air Quality in Residential Buildings).

q: What does ASHRAE mean?
o: Alliance for Safe HVAC and Refrigeration Applications and Efficiency
Association for Sustainable Heating, Refrigeration, and Air Engineering
Advanced Standards for Heating, Airflow, and Refrigeration Engineering
American Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air-Conditioning Engineers
n: ASHRAE stands for the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers. Source: ASHRAE (official name and charter).

q: In terms of compressive strength, steel is about how many times stronger than concrete?
n: Structural steel's compressive strength (about 250–400 MPa) is roughly ten times that of ordinary structural concrete (about 21–35 MPa). Source: NSCP 2015, Ch. 4 and Ch. 5 (material properties); Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction.
